balance.argument_a: Route A wins on this case's stated figures: 55.3 minutes saved per traveler vs. driving, at $289,145/year, for 0.24849 minutes saved per dollar -- both endpoints already have the airline's ground infrastructure, and the route replaces a genuinely painful 3-leg existing-network alternative that almost nobody actually uses.
balance.argument_b: Route B is close behind at 0.21442 minutes saved per dollar (15.89% behind A) despite serving a smaller, currently-nonexistent market -- it creates air access from nothing, costs less to operate (shorter route, fewer block hours), and its case rests entirely on whether Cortland County's real ~46,246 population can plausibly support the same 25-traveler/week estimate this case applies equally to both routes.
balance.margin_basis: (shared weekly travelers x minutes saved per traveler vs. driving x 52) / annual operating cost, for A and B, using Appendix B-E's sourced/derived figures and Appendix F's shared ground-overhead and ridership assumptions.

sensitivity_disclosure.justification: Ground-time overhead for a route that has never flown is a genuine forecast/irreducible unknown -- no public per-flight ground-time figure exists for this fictional airline's specific small airports, and no amount of research pins down the true value before the route actually operates. The winner (Route A) never flips across the full +/-50% range (22.5-67.5 min), but at the high end (67.5 min) the margin widens to 71.0%, exceeding SPEC section 2's 20% cap for that flexed point specifically -- disclosed here rather than hidden. The case's OWN reported base value (45 min, margin 15.89%) stays comfortably within the 20% cap; only the flexed extreme breaches it, and the winner is unaffected even there.

sensitivity_note: See FACILITATOR.md Robustness Check: ground-time overhead (MA1) swept +/-50%, winner (Route A) stable across the entire range (margin 1.99%-41.53%). Shared ridership assumption (MA2) provably cancels out of the A-vs-B ratio and cannot flip the winner.
